summary: American radio host Rush Limbaugh rose from Missouri DJ to the most influential conservative voice in the US from the late 1980s until his 2021 death, spreading racist, misogynist and conspiratorial rhetoric that reshaped the Republican right.

evidence.note: born in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, January 1951
hired in Sacramento to replace Morton Downey Jr.; start of right-wing persona
moves to New York and launches the national show in 1988
AIDS Update segment mocking gay men dying of AIDS
end of the Fairness Doctrine as precondition for his national career
TV show produced with Roger Ailes, framed as test run for Fox News
misogynist bits and anti-feminist rhetoric discussed at length
opioid addiction scandal 2003-2006 versus his drug-war rhetoric
extended run of racist on-air bits and quotes
courted by Bush, role in the 1994 Republican Revolution
pushes Vince Foster murder conspiracy and mainstreams fringe theories
neo-Nazi podcasters mourn him; host argues he prepared the right for fascism

notes: main_span starts in 1984 with the Sacramento KFBK job (year from general knowledge; transcript says mid-1980s) and ends with his February 2021 death. Grandfather Rush Sr. and Missouri family background get only a few minutes, so covered_span follows the lifetime rule from 1951. Climate denial and Covid denial get brief mentions only, so environmental-destruction and public-health were left out.
